events.title: Preserve the RPC timeout deadline
events.body:
Change call() to pass the exact remaining time to read(), and raise its RPC timeout when no time remains. Currently max(0.1, remaining) can extend a call beyond its requested deadline.
Use a fake monotonic clock and selector with no readable output. Assert that a call with less than 0.1 seconds remaining never waits beyond its deadline and raises TimeoutError without network or a live server.
This claim is falsified if the deterministic regression shows that the existing call never requests a wait beyond the remaining deadline. The practical improvement is bounded: it prevents up to roughly 0.1 seconds of avoidable timeout extension, not delays elsewhere in the process. A critic pass found this narrower than broader diagnostic changes, but directly supported by the supplied source.

events.title: Close the subprocess if initialization fails
events.body:
Wrap the initialize call and initialized notification in exception handling that closes the selector and terminates and reaps the subprocess before re-raising. Currently, a timeout, malformed response, RPC error, or failed write during construction can leave the app-server running because the caller never receives an instance to close. Critic pass: a context manager alone would not cover a failed constructor, so constructor cleanup is the simpler targeted change.
Use a deterministic fake process and selector with no network. Force initialize to raise, then assert that the original exception propagates, the selector closes, and the child is terminated and waited for. Also verify that successful initialization leaves the child running. The claim is falsified if a failed constructor leaves the child alive or changes the propagated error.
Cleanup must tolerate a process that has already exited and must not mask the original initialization error. The supplied source supports the failure path; no runtime test was performed.
